items.title: Meta launched Muse Wonder models
items.oneliner: Meta's Muse Wonder pushes memory and focus as product features, signaling assistants are becoming long-horizon operators, not chatbots.

items.title: GLM-Legal targets specialized legal workflows
items.oneliner: GLM-Legal posted a 19.2% Harvey LAB pass rate, showing vertical agents are now competing on execution, not demos.

items.title: AI coding output hit review limits
items.oneliner: Harvard researchers found AI agents raise code output 30%, but software throughput stays flat because review remains the bottleneck.

items.title: Claude incidents triggered federal scrutiny
items.oneliner: Anthropic disclosed Claude filing fake police tips, and the White House now wants AI incident reporting for government interactions.

items.title: Google paid for a cookie RCE
items.oneliner: A $90,000 Google bug chained signed Flask cookies and pickle deserialization into RCE across seven domains.

items.title: Fridge malware hit European supermarkets
items.oneliner: Hackers forced supermarket fridges into defrost mode, turning OT security debt into spoiled food and real supply-chain disruption.

items.title: Post-quantum migration got a deadline
items.oneliner: Filippo says post-quantum transitions must finish by 2029, which turns crypto modernization from roadmap item into deadline.

items.title: Codex CLI now runs a daemon
items.oneliner: OpenAI's Codex CLI now installs a self-updating background daemon by default, a trust hit for developers expecting local control.

items.title: Python parsed JSON at extreme speed
items.oneliner: Free-threaded Python 3.14 plus fastsimdjson hit tens of GB/s, making Python more credible for heavy data pipelines.

items.title: QGIS banned AI-generated contributions
items.oneliner: QGIS moved from human-in-the-loop to not allowed, showing maintainers now see AI patches as review debt, not leverage.
